summary: A monthly report of ARPANET traffic for November 1973. It tabulates, for each Host, how many packets it sent, split between traffic that stayed within its own node and traffic sent to other nodes, with daily averages. It is a data memo and defines no protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 601 reports how many packets ARPANET Hosts sent in November 1973. Its table separates packets sent between nodes from packets sent within a node.

questions: how much traffic did the arpanet carry in november 1973
how many inter-node packets were sent in november 1973
subtitle: Host-by-host ARPANET packet output statistics for November 1973.

tldr.problem: This report records packets output by ARPANET Hosts during November 1973.
tldr.mechanism: The attached table separates inter-node and intra-node packet counts and lists totals and daily averages for individual Hosts and sites.
tldr.outcome: RFC 601 is a traffic report, not a protocol specification, and the unit metadata says it updates RFC 586.

today: The unit records RFC 601's status as Unknown and says it updates RFC 586. It reports Host traffic statistics for November 1973.

sections.title: November Host Traffic
sections.content:
Alex McKenzie attaches the Host traffic statistics for November 1973. The attachment is a Host Throughput Summary of packets output, organized by network site and Host number.

For sites with more than one Host, the table shows individual Host rows and a site subtotal. It also gives daily averages and the number of days counted.
sections.plainLanguage: The table lists packets sent by each Host during November 1973. When a site has several Hosts, it also gives a combined site count.

sections.title: Inter-Node and Intra-Node Counts
sections.content:
Each row divides packets output into inter-node and intra-node counts, then gives a total. The table provides a daily average alongside the number of days included in the report for that row or subtotal.

Several sites are explicitly marked as having no traffic. The report presents counts but does not explain why individual Hosts sent different amounts.
sections.plainLanguage: Inter-node packets go between nodes; intra-node packets stay within a node. The table adds both types and shows a daily average.

sections.title: The Report's Totals
sections.content:
The final summary reports 85,314,100 inter-node packets and 23,971,670 intra-node packets. It gives daily averages of 2,843,803 and 799,056 respectively, and an internode packets/messages value of 1.08.

These are the totals and averages printed in the attached table for November 1973.
sections.plainLanguage: The last rows total the two kinds of traffic across the listed Hosts. They also show daily averages and a packets-to-messages figure for inter-node traffic.

references.text: McKenzie, A., Traffic Statistics (October 1973), RFC 586, updated by this RFC.
